Then this song will be celebrated perfectly, when the joy of the whole Church is complete.

These two words, “Alleluia” and “Amen,” are Hebrew. They can indeed be translated: “Alleluia” means “Praise the Lord,” while “Amen” is rendered as “faith” or “truth.” Nevertheless, out of reverence for the holiness of that first language, their authority is preserved. The Church therefore continually sings “Alleluia” on Sundays and throughout the period of Pentecost, because of the hope of the resurrection that will be fulfilled in the Lord’s praise. “Amen,” however, is properly spoken by the devotion of the faithful in response to the priest’s supplication or blessing, in order to obtain that same perpetual life—or every good thing that one hopes to receive from the Lord, whether in the present or in the future.

The arrangement of these words therefore suitably belongs to the holy cross, because through it the confession of all things united in the praise of the Lord has been established, the number of angels is completed, the heavenly army is increased, the people of the saints are gathered, access to eternal life is granted them, and the ancient curse is dissolved because a new blessing is created.

Accordingly, in the book just mentioned, the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures sang a new song to the Lamb, saying:

“Worthy are you, Lord God, to receive the book and to open its seals, because you were slain and redeemed us for God by your blood, from every tribe and language and people and nation, and made us a kingdom and priests for our God, and they shall reign upon the earth.”

“And I saw and heard the voice of many angels surrounding the throne and the living creatures and the elders; and their number was thousands upon thousands, saying with a loud voice:

‘Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power and divinity and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing, and every creature that is in heaven and upon the earth and under the earth, and those that are in the sea and all that are in it.’ I heard them all saying: ‘To the one seated upon the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and power for ever and ever.’ And the four living creatures said: ‘Amen.’”

The following verse is written in the “Alleluia,” and is to be read through the sequence of the letters of that word:

> Eternal cross, you are the praise of God; you live in the citadel of heaven.

“Amen,” too, begins with its four letters through the four horns of the cross, first proceeding from “Alleluia,” which is completed by eight letters.

## FIGURE XXVI. On the sayings of the prophets that pertain to Christ’s passion and to our redemption

[Col. 0251]

[Col. 0251A]

> Therefore the utterance of the prophets rightly honors you, cross,  
> Proclaims and exalts you, and resounds with your future deeds.  
> What the people then uttered with inspired mouth,  
> The Holy Spirit had inwardly commanded them.  
> They speak of all things when they say that Christ will restore them,  
> And that, fastened upon you, the Lord will grant kingdoms to the gentle.  
> David had said that his palms and feet would be pierced,  
> And that gall would be given as food and vinegar as drink;  
> From your wood he declares him to be king over all.  
> Isaiah declares that dominion is upon the shoulders of this child;  
> He foresees his body struck, his hands extended,  
> His blessed face spat upon, his death and suffering,  
> And Israel, scattered, raised up and running toward you.  
> Jeremiah describes a lamb, as though a holy burnt offering,  
> Led away without a voice and destined to be fed upon wood.  
> Ezekiel sees in a vision the sign of the letter Tau  
> Rescuing the people, after the likeness of a cross being carried.  
> Thus, holy salvation, you were seen by the prophets as power:  
> [Col. 0251B] You are pleasing to the heavenly ones, cross; you are a sailor [or: ship] for this world.  
> [Col. 0252A] For Daniel said that Christ would here be punished by an evil people  
> And that thereafter all guilt would reach its end.  
> Hosea proclaims that the people will be saved through the death of death,  
> And Joel had foretold that hour.  
> Both sun and stars would not pour out their light upon the earth:  
> Amos, too, had foretold this in an ill-omened festival.  
> Obadiah depicted the ambushes, and Jonah the funeral.  
> Micah, the mountain of God; Nahum announces what vengeance is.  
> Habakkuk proclaims with his mouth the horns of the holy cross,  
> And Zephaniah hears from long ago the bitter day of the Lord.  
> Haggai said that heaven and earth would be shaken;  
> Zechariah notes Jesus in filthy garments, the wounds fixed in his hands, and many mourning.  
> Malachi sees the supreme one ruling throughout the world, and the world and the ministers perspiring at the burning fire.  
> These deeds of yours the worthy men of old proclaimed with their mouths,  
> O nourishing cross, prophet and author; in these things  
> [Col. 0252B] You, holy passion of Christ, fulfill all these things. [Col. 0253]

## EXPLANATION OF THE FIGURE

[Col. 0253A]

On this page I have wished to gather certain testimonies from the sayings of the prophets that were prophesied concerning Christ’s passion and that extend to the glory of the holy cross. Although many such passages can be found, the brevity of this little work prevents us from marking all of them here. We have nevertheless introduced those that came most readily to mind while dictating and that could most easily be found by someone seeking them.

The prophet and psalmist David has many testimonies of this kind. Concerning the manner of the Lord’s passion, he says in Psalm 22, speaking in the person of Christ:

“They pierced my hands and my feet; they counted all my bones. They themselves looked upon and observed me; they divided my garments among themselves, and upon my clothing they cast lots.”

And again in Psalm 69:

“They gave gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.”

That he would suffer upon wood he shows in Psalm 145, saying:

“Let all the earth be moved before his face; say among the nations: ‘The Lord shall reign from the wood,’” and so forth.

Isaiah likewise says:

“For a child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and the government has been made upon his shoulder,” and so forth.

And again:

“On that day there shall be a root of Jesse, who stands as a sign for the peoples; the nations shall entreat him, and his tomb shall be glorious.”

A little later:

“He will raise a sign among the nations, and will gather the fugitives of Israel and collect the dispersed of Judah from the four quarters of the earth,” and so forth.

And again:

“The Lord laid upon him the iniquity of us all. He was offered because he himself willed it, and he did not open his mouth. Like a sheep he will be led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer he will become silent, and he will not open his mouth.”

And again, speaking in the person of the Lord:

“I gave my body to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who tore at them. I did not turn my face away from those who rebuked and spat upon me,” and so forth.

And again:

“I stretched out my hands all day long toward an unbelieving people who walk in a way that is not good, following their own thoughts.”

Jeremiah, speaking in the person of the Lord, says:

“I was like a gentle lamb that is carried to the sacrifice, and I did not know that they devised schemes against me, saying: ‘Let us put wood into his bread and wipe him from the land of the living, so that his name may no longer be remembered.’”

And again:

“The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, has been captured in our sins.”

Ezekiel expressed the sign of the cross in the figure of the letter T, saying:

“And he said to the man clothed in linen: ‘Pass through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and mark a Tau upon the foreheads of the men who groan and grieve over all the abominations that are committed in its midst,’” and so forth.

And, expressing that good shepherd who laid down his life for his sheep, he says:

“Thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I myself will seek my sheep and visit them. As a shepherd visits his flock on the day when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will visit my sheep and deliver them from all the places in which they were dispersed, on the day of cloud and darkness. I will lead them out from the peoples, gather them from the lands, bring them into their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel.’”

And a little later:

“I myself will feed my sheep and make them lie down, says the Lord. I will seek what was lost, bring back what had been cast away, bind up what was broken, strengthen what was weak, guard what was fat and strong, and feed them with judgment.”

Daniel, the most reliable chronicler, faithfully disclosed the time of the Lord’s incarnation and our redemption, with an angel revealing this to him. He says:

“Seventy weeks have been shortened concerning your people and your holy city, so that transgression may be completed, sin may come to an end, iniquity may be blotted out, everlasting righteousness may be brought in, and vision and prophecy may be fulfilled, and the Holy of Holies may be anointed.”

“Know therefore and understand: from the going forth of the word that Jerusalem be rebuilt until Christ the prince, there shall be seven and sixty-two weeks.”

A little later he adds:

“After sixty-two weeks Christ shall be killed, and he shall not be; and the people with the coming prince shall destroy the city and the sanctuary.”

And, to show that the week of years in which Christ preached the Gospel and performed miracles, and in which he suffered and rose from the dead, surpassed the others, he speaks of it separately:

“He will confirm sin for many for one week, and in the middle of the week sacrifice and offering shall fail; and in the temple there shall be the abomination of desolation, and desolation shall continue until the consummation and the end.”

Hosea also most clearly proclaims the devotion of the nations and the gathering together of the Church assembled through Christ:

“It shall be in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ that they shall be called ‘sons of the living God.’ And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint one head for themselves,” and so forth.

And concerning our rescue from hell and the destruction of death, he declares the Lord’s promise, saying:

“I will deliver them from the hand of death; I will redeem them from death. I shall be your death, O death; I shall be your sting, O hell.”

Joel demonstrates the Lord’s passion and the salvation of the faithful, saying:

“The sun and the moon were darkened, and the stars withdrew their light. The Lord will roar from Zion, and from Jerusalem he will give his voice; heaven and earth will be shaken. The Lord is the hope of his people and the strength of the children of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling upon my holy mountain; Jerusalem shall be holy, and strangers shall no longer pass through it,” and so forth.

Amos says:

“It shall be on that day, says the Lord, that the sun will go down at noon and I will darken the earth in the day of light; I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into lamentation,” and so forth.

A little later:

“On that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that has fallen, rebuild its breaches, restore what had collapsed,” and so forth.

Obadiah, expressing the treacheries of the Jews against the Lord and the salvation of the Church, says:

“All the men of your covenant have deceived you; the men of your peace have prevailed against you; those who eat with you will lay ambushes beneath you,” and so forth.

A little later:

“Upon Mount Zion there shall be salvation, and it shall be holy; and the house of Jacob shall possess those who had possessed them.”

And again he adds:

“The Savior shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom shall belong to the Lord.”

The Lord himself also revealed Jonah’s prophecy, saying:

“As Jonah was in the belly of the whale for three days and three nights, so the Son of Man shall be in the heart of the earth.”

Micah proclaims the gathering of the peoples to Christ, showing him to be the mountain and ruler of the Lord:

“In the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared upon the summit of the mountains,” and so forth.

And again:

“But you, Bethlehem Ephratha, though you are little among the thousands of Judah, from you shall go forth for me a ruler who shall be governor in Israel,” and so forth.

Nahum proclaims the Lord as avenger against his enemies and good toward the devout and his friends:

“God is jealous and the Lord takes vengeance; the Lord takes vengeance and possesses wrath; the Lord takes vengeance upon his enemies and is angry with his foes,” and so forth.

And, showing his compassion, he says:

“The Lord is good and strengthens in the day of tribulation, and knows those who hope in him.”

Habakkuk, a strong and stern watcher, stands upon his watch and fixes his step upon the fortification, so that he may contemplate Christ upon the cross and say:

“His glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise. His splendor shall be like the light; horns are in his hands. There his strength is hidden.”

Zephaniah recounts that the day of the Lord and the hour of his passion and resurrection are near:

“The great day of the Lord is near; it is near and comes very swiftly. The voice of the day of the Lord is bitter; there the mighty man shall be afflicted.”

And a little later:

“I will afflict men, and they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the Lord.”

And again:

“Therefore wait for me, says the Lord, on the day of my resurrection in the future,” and so forth.

Haggai announces the one desired by all nations:

“Yet a little while, says the Lord, and I will shake heaven and earth and the sea and the dry land,” and so forth.

Zechariah, remembering his Lord, sees Jesus in filthy garments, and the stone with seven eyes, and the golden lampstand, and so forth.

He also says in the person of the Lord:

“They weighed out my wages at thirty pieces of silver.”

And again:

“I will pour out upon the house of David the spirit of grace and supplication, and they will look upon me whom they pierced, and they will mourn for him with a mourning like that for an only son,” and so forth.

And again:

“Adam is my likeness from my youth,” and it shall be said: “‘What are these wounds in the midst of your hands?’ And he shall say: ‘With these I was wounded in the house of those who loved me.’”

“Awake, sword, against my shepherd and against the man who is joined to me, says the Lord of hosts. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered.”

And again:

“The Lord shall be king over all the earth. On that day the Lord shall be one, and his name shall be one.”

Malachi recounts the saving advent of the Lord:

“Immediately, says he, the ruler whom you seek and the angel of the covenant whom you desire shall come to his temple; behold, he comes, says the Lord of hosts. And who can think of the day of his coming, and who can stand to see him? For he is like a refining fire and like fuller’s herb. He will sit refining and cleansing silver, purify the sons of Levi, and refine them like gold and silver; and they shall offer sacrifices to the Lord in righteousness. Then the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem shall be pleasing to God,” and so forth.

[Col. 0256C]

The following verse of thirty-seven letters is written upon the cross:

> You are pleasing to the heavenly ones, O cross; you are a sailor for this world.

It is a hexameter when read in the ordinary direction, and, with no syllable omitted, becomes the same pentameter when read in reverse.

## FIGURE XXVII. On the sayings of the apostles concerning the same subject in the New Testament

[Col. 0257]

[Col. 0257A]

> No less faithfully, therefore, your character preserves the rights  
> Of the New Testament, and unfolds the holy gifts  
> Which the high God, divine man, brought to the world.  
> Through you, sacred cross, venerated with frequent vows,  
> He fulfills the promise and the truthful doctrines of the prophets,  
> Testifying that he is Lord of both the Old and the New Law,  
> Who by a twofold word opened the abyss to the world.  
> By his deed he gladdens us, satisfying the hopes of those before us;  
> He who consoled them is truthful, good, and just toward all.  
> Therefore the apostolic word, faithful in righteous utterances,  
> Praises everywhere your gracious trophies, O cross.  
> Peter, prince throughout the world, sounds forth from his inmost heart,  
> Thus, devoutly, he speaks your praises, O best one:  
> “Christ suffered for you upon the wood,  
> Leaving you a clear example, so that you may follow  
> [Col. 0257B] His footsteps, whose sacred wounds bring healing.”  
> Hence I believe that Jesus receives the words of one who prays,  
> If I strive for him, and if honor proceeds toward him in songs:  
> [Col. 0258A] Because he is gentle, these gifts are not contemptible to him.  
> James likewise exhorts us here with pure speech,  
> Setting forth Christ as an example at the end of labors.  
> From here the lofty leader John also admonishes us in writing:  
> May chaste love remain and make sober vows serene—  
> Jesus, who devoutly suffered for love.  
> Thus may we, with devout mind, suffer in joined love; here  
> He piously sings Jesus, the true Jesus through the type.  
> Jude [presents] the leader to the faithful and the wicked.  
> Paul, too, prayed a little while ago, bearing you in his mouth,  
> Sacred cross, when he said that he already knew no speech  
> Without you, nor knew how to offer any praise with his throat:  
> Your great name in heaven, on earth, and through Tartarus—  
> For Christ’s sake he promises that you are fully worthy.  
> Thus the apostolic order also praises you in harmony.  
> [Col. 0252B] You join all things, captured from the ancient prophets.  
> Holy passion of pious Jesus, through the ages of Christ. [Col. 0259]

## EXPLANATION OF THE FIGURE

[Col. 0259A]

The examples of writings in the New Testament concerning the saving passion and resurrection of our Lord are so abundant that it is not easy to select the clearest testimonies from so great a multitude. One does not know which to choose, since there are so many that they cannot be gathered into a single little book; and all possess such dignity that even the learned cannot adequately judge which among them are clearer and more authoritative.

But just as from the Old Testament—that is, from the books of the prophets—we selected certain passages that foretold the Lord’s future passion, which had not yet been completed, so from the New Testament we select only those that are suitable for proclaiming the magnificence and praise of the holy cross and that pertain to glorifying the goodness of the Creator and the mercy of our Redeemer on behalf of our liberation.

What those earlier writers foretold as future, these proclaim as already accomplished and completed. For the acts of the holy cross ought to be proclaimed from both Testaments, because Christ is the dispenser and mediator of both. He himself invisibly governed the minds of the prophets through the inspiration of his Spirit; then, assuming a visible body, he taught the apostles by words and examples—he who had promised salvation and life to his people through the patriarchs and prophets.

Having become man, he fulfilled the promise through the power of his cross. Through the prophet he said:

“Strengthen the weak hands and make firm the feeble knees. Say to the fainthearted: ‘Take courage; do not fear. Behold, your God will bring the vengeance of recompense; God himself will come and save you,’” and so forth.

The apostle Peter shows that this has already happened when he says:

“You know, brothers, what took place throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John preached: Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power; how he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with him. And we are witnesses of all that he did in the region of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him upon a tree; God raised him on the third day and granted that he be made manifest—not to all the people, but to witnesses preordained by God, to us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead. And he commanded us to preach and testify that he is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. To him all the prophets bear witness, that through his name all who believe in him receive remission.”

The same Peter says something similar in his Epistle:

“Christ died once for our sins, the just for the unjust, so that he might offer us to God, put to death indeed in the flesh but made alive in the spirit.”

And again:

“Christ suffered for us, leaving you an example so that you might follow his footsteps.”

A little later he adds:

“He handed himself over to the one who judges justly. He himself bore our sins in his body upon the wood, so that, having died to sins, we might live to righteousness; by whose bruising you have been healed.”

James, the Lord’s brother, likewise exhorts us to the same example, saying:

“Take the prophets, who spoke in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, as an example of labor and patience. Behold, we call blessed those who endured. You have heard of the patience of Job and have seen the end of the Lord, because the Lord is compassionate and merciful.”

The apostle John gives us confidence in his mercy, saying:

“My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; and he is the propitiation for our sins—not for ours only, but also for those of the whole world.”

And again:

“In this we have known the love of God: that he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.”

The apostle Jude, the brother of James, showed by the example of Moses’ successor that Jesus Christ led us through the cross out of the spiritual Egypt—that is, from the power of darkness—and destroyed the unbelievers, saying:

“I wish to remind you, though you know all things once for all, that Jesus, having saved the people from the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe. The angels who did not preserve their own principality but abandoned their dwelling he has reserved under darkness in everlasting chains for the judgment of the great day.”

The apostle Paul, teacher of the nations, who was the last of all the apostles in his calling but labored more than all the others, is so varied in his speech when commending to us Christ’s passion, resurrection, and redemption through his blood and his dominion in heaven and on earth that he seems almost entirely occupied with this subject.

Since he ought not to be excluded from this praise—he who wrote more about Christ than all the others and is so well suited to it that his testimony can readily be condensed into a short space, with the rest omitted—we shall nevertheless set down the testimonies that he especially applied to the cross.

He says to the Corinthians:

“Christ did not send me to baptize but to evangelize, not in the wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of power. For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those who are being saved—that is, to us—it is the power of God,” and so forth.

And again:

“I judged that I knew nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.”

To the Galatians he says:

“Far be it from me to glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.”

To the Ephesians:

“He is our peace, who made both one and destroyed the dividing wall of hostility in his flesh, abolishing the law of commandments expressed in decrees, so that he might create the two in himself as one new man, making peace, and reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, killing the hostility in himself,” and so forth.

To the Philippians:

“Christ humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross. Therefore God also exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name,” and so forth.

To the Colossians, proclaiming Christ’s majesty, he says:

“In him all things were created, those in heaven and those on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things were created through him and in him. He is before all things, and all things hold together in him. He is the head of the body, the Church; he is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he might hold first place in everything. For in him all the fullness of divinity was pleased to dwell, and through him to reconcile all things to himself, making peace by the blood of his cross, whether those on earth or those in heaven.”

And again, in the same Epistle:

“He forgave us all our offenses, blotting out the record of debt that stood against us in decrees and was hostile to us; he removed it from our midst, fastening it to the cross,” and so forth.

In the Apocalypse also, nearly all the praises and songs contained in it are suited to proclaiming the glory of Christ’s passion and the grace of our redemption, since the book itself repeatedly speaks openly of the slain Lamb who is in the midst of the throne. We have judged it unnecessary to place some of those testimonies here, because we have inserted no few of them elsewhere in this book.

Two heroic verses are also written here in the image of the holy cross, using the same letters. The first, written along the length of the cross, is:

> If you give me gifts, Jesus, I will sound these measures for you in songs. [Text uncertain.]

But when it is read with the same letters—that is, from its end back to its beginning—it produces this verse, written across the cross:

> If you give gifts to him, and if honor goes to him, he will fashion [or: restore] art and songs. [Text uncertain.]

When read backward through the same letters, it returns to the first verse, namely, the one written along the length of the cross.

[Col. 0261]

## FIGURE XXVIII. On the craftsman’s adoration of the cross

[Col. 0261A]

> Almighty power, lofty majesty, Sabaoth,  
> Most high Lord, supreme creator of powers,  
> Fashioner of the world, truly the Redeemer of humankind:  
> You are my praise, my power, my glory, my all, and my salvation;  
> You are king, teacher, ruler, dear master;  
> You are the shepherd who feeds and the true protector of the fold.  
> You are also my portion, holy Savior and author,  
> Leader, way, light, life, good reward, and gate of the kingdom;  
> Voice, understanding, word, joyful offspring of virtues.  
> Toward you I have directed, and now direct, my words in abundance;  
> My mind speaks of you, the whole intention of my mind,  
> [Col. 0262A] Whatever the tongue, the hand, and the blessed mouth pray,  
> The humble heart, the upright life, the consecrated will.  
> All things praise and sing of you, serene Christ.  
> For I, bowed down and joyful, adore you as Lord,  
> And here I humbly address your cross in salutation:  
> “I ask you for hope; may I take up the altar as a branch [text uncertain], and here I pray.”  
> This is my clear ardor; this is the fire of love;  
> This my mind first seeks; this my speech and my prayers;  
> This is the thirst of my soul, the great desire to eat:  
> That you, merciful and good Christ, may receive me through the altar  
> As an offered servant, so that I may be your victim, Jesus.  
> [Col. 0263A] May I be your sacrifice; may my whole self be crucified  
> And now consumed by you; may your passion calm the heat  
> Of the flesh, shatter vices, suppress anger,  
> Bridle the tongue, and restore words of piety.  
> May it pacify the mind and lead life in righteousness.  
> For when your fiery coming shines throughout Olympus,  
> The heat will scorch the wicked; the storm will roar,  
> The horn will already bellow, and the sign of the cross  
> Will appear before the world in the air.  
> Then I pray that the cross itself rescue me from avenging flames  
> And that it defend from wrath the proper poet of the Lamb,  
> [Col. 0264A] To whom I sing—I shall rightly sing, Hrabanus, with mouth in verse,  
> With heart and hand, always, in memorable song:  
> For he had graciously given me a memorable gift upon the altar of life.  
> When merciful Jesus himself rescues me from the depths  
> Of hell’s pyre, now, O Christ, from the citadel of heaven  
> Grant me this, I ask, I hope, and truly believe all  
> That you promised; I hold to this with piety and faith.  
> For you, being truthful, make all things true according to the order of judgment.  
> Go now to the realms above; rightly triumph in heaven.  
> O gracious praise of the cross, farewell forever without end. [Col. 0263]

## EXPLANATION OF THE FIGURE
[Col. 0263A] Almighty God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who willed that your Only-Begotten Son, born before the ages, should assume human flesh and soul in time and undergo the cross for the salvation of the human race: I adore you and give you thanks, because you granted me, your wretched servant [Col. 0263B] (although unworthy and weighed down by the burden of many crimes), your grace, so that by singing and writing down the passion of your beloved Son in praise—though not worthily, yet devoutly—I might proclaim it.

To you, Lord Jesus Christ, Only-Begotten Son of God, I offer humble prayers and pay the vows of my lips, because you have deigned to inspire me to sing, however inadequately, the honor of your holy cross and to preach to my fellow servants the common salvation of us all. Nor did consciousness of my own sins hold me back from what I had begun; rather, it gave me greater confidence that I should celebrate in this poem the one in which you destroyed the reign of sin and granted forgiveness for all offenses to the whole world.

To you, Holy Spirit, the Comforter, I render thanks with all my inmost heart, [Col. 0263C] because you have deigned by your grace to assist and console me in the work itself. I beseech you: if, through my weakness, I have set down anything unsuitable or have not rightly understood anything, may you deign to enlighten me by your visitation, so that I may correct it fittingly and through you obtain forgiveness for my error; and may you, whom I called upon for help before beginning the work, bring me without shipwreck to the desired shore.

You, eternal and everlasting God, Trinity and inseparable Unity, I worship, adore, seek, and desire with all my heart, all my soul, all my mind, and all my strength. You are my illumination, my salvation, my praise, my strength; creator, redeemer, restorer, father, judge, teacher, blessedness, fortitude, joy, eternity, happiness, serenity; one almighty God, God of gods, Lord, creator of all things, [Col. 0263D] God, light and life of the faithful, living life, life from the Living One, giver of life to the living, loving and beloved, and most loving love; begetter and begotten, powerfully regenerating; speaker, Word, and proceeding from both; [Col. 0264A] loving and beloved, and the love of both; true light, light from light, true illumination, counselor, counsel, and communion. From you, through you, and in you are all things. To you be praise and glory for everlasting ages.

I ask you, most merciful Father, that since you first [Col. 0264B] willed me to complete this work by writing it, which pertains to the praise of our Redeemer and Savior, I may through him deserve to obtain the grace of his redemption and salvation. Whatever work I undertake thereafter, cause it all to proceed from your grace, through your grace, and in your grace, to your praise; and command that I thereafter be safer from sins and stronger in good works. As long as I live in this little body, may I always offer you some service. After my soul’s departure from the body, grant me through him forgiveness of all sins and the reception of eternal life—through him who, with you and the Holy Spirit, lives and reigns as God, equal to you, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

[Col. 0264C] On the cross of the preceding page there is written one verse of twenty-seven letters, which can be read and reread using those same letters in this manner:

**Oro te ramus aram ara sumar et oro**  
“I pray to you, O branch; altar, altar: may I be taken up, and I pray.”

The image of myself, which I had painted beneath the cross, bending my knees and praying, is composed in Asclepiadic meter. The first verse is a heroic hexameter, and the second a hemistich of a heroic verse, as follows:

**Rabanum memet clemens rogo, Christe, tuere,**  
**O pie judicio.**

“Merciful Christ, I ask you to protect me, Rabanus,  
O pious one in judgment.”

This entire book contains twenty-eight metrical figures, each followed by its prose, excluding the title page and the prologue. That number is perfect within the hundred by its parts; therefore I wished to complete the work according to its sum, since in it I sang of that form which is the consummation and perfection of things.

# BOOK TWO

[Col. 0265]

## PREFACE

[Col. 0265A]

It was the custom among the ancients to compose their works in a double style, so that their writings might at once be more pleasing and more useful to readers. Hence among both secular and ecclesiastical authors many are found who have described one and the same subject in meter and prose. To say nothing of others, what else are Prosper and the venerable Sedulius seen to have done? Did they not for this reason publish their work in two forms, using the two styles, so that the variety itself might remove weariness from readers, and so that if someone understood something less clearly in one form, he might immediately recognize it more fully explained in the other?

Following this example and for this reason, I, a most insignificant little man, took care to turn into prose the work that I composed in metrical style in praise of the holy cross, so that [Col. 0265B] since, because of the difficulty of its order and the demands of its figures, the language seems obscure and its meaning less open in meter, at least in prose it might become clearer. I was not striving to speak in this work with the same words that I had used in meter, but with the same meaning. The sharp and learned Horace likewise instructed the educated translator in the *Art of Poetry*, saying:

> You will not take care, as a faithful  
> translator, to render word for word.

For in a certain sense I am a translator in this work—not from one language into another, but from one mode of expression into another—in order to explain the truth of the same meaning.

Therefore I ask the reader not to receive our labor disdainfully. Let him know that I do not wish to devote myself to excess [Col. 0265C] but to usefulness; nor do I wish to begrudge anyone anything, but rather, in brotherly charity, to contribute by writing for the benefit of my neighbor whatever I am able to do by divine grace. May the goodness of almighty God grant me to accomplish in deed whatever good I hold in my mind; and may everyone who receives our labor in a brotherly spirit, by God’s gift, share with us in eternal joy.

**The Preface ends.**

## CHAPTER ONE  
### On the first figure, in which the image of Christ extends its hands in the form of a cross

Behold the Son of God and Lord of lords, displaying here, with his hands extended, the venerable form of the Restorer. And rightly does the holy flock of the Church worship this one shepherd as just; and in the very manner in which he permitted his limbs to be stretched upon his cross, all peoples rightly acknowledge the Redeemer, because sacred Scripture proclaims him to be the father of all authority.

Recognizing this also, though unworthy, I adore according to my measure the summit of all heights, the Lord Jesus, and I believe that he is the King of kings. But Judea, which, goaded by envy, is the inventor of evil, wickedly killed its own king. Yet he [Col. 0266A] rose again in glory and, according to the prophets’ promise, powerfully overturned the weapons of the wicked through the word of his Gospel.

But let us who believe in him rejoice in him, while anyone who does not confess him to be the eternal Lord doubts wickedly and disastrously. For this is the author of all things, worshiped throughout the whole world, to whom all things ought to be subject; for the right hand of the most high Father, righteous and holy, rescued the offered prey from the depths of hell by his blood, and, placed in this manner upon the cross, granted the heavenly kingdom to his faithful.

Here he is the beginning of all things; here God is with us; here he is the origin and end of the universe, true light, the image of the invisible God the Father, the mouth of the Lord, the splendor of eternal light. Consubstantial with the Father, he is the sun of justice, the Word of God, and light from light. Here [Col. 0266B] he is the coequal power and hand of the Lord, leader of the righteous and true prophet, whom we rightly confess to be the Only-Begotten and Firstborn Son of God. He is the cornerstone for believers, but for unbelievers the stone of offense and rock of stumbling; and he is likewise the door of life.

Behold, I shall explain what Christ, clothed in a garment, signifies mystically. Christ’s garment is also the divine law, which, in the poor covering of letters, in a certain way embraces the author who contains all things. To him belong the whole world, heaven and earth, the sea, and the entire creation; he who measures heaven in his fist and encloses the earth in his palm.

Likewise, our nature, which he assumed for our redemption, is as though a garment of his divinity. For it conceals the radiance of his majesty from human sight; [Col. 0266C] hiding and enclosing the rays of his splendor before the eyes of the wicked. Yet through flashing miracles and the thundering Gospel he made himself known as the true God.

He is also the angel of great counsel, sent to God’s people with supreme devotion: teaching with wisdom, the peaceful guardian, the fountain of eternal life, the arm of the Lord, and the living bread that came down from heaven. Christ is the rock, the morning star rising, and the true physician; the key of David, the way of life, and the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world; the serpent who, when lifted up, gives life to those who are dying; the mediator between God and human beings, worm and man, leading captivity captive; the mountain of God, the high-soaring eagle, our advocate.

He is the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the good shepherd, and the kid bearing our sins; the foundation of faith, the innocent sheep, the priest according to [Col. 0266D] the order of Melchizedek, offering bread and wine. For he was sacrificed for us as a calf and a ram. He who is the Son of the eternal Father was himself condemned to the punishment of the wood. He was begotten from the Father’s womb before the morning star and before every creature; and in time he came forth in an instant from his mother’s womb. To save the human race, Christ the eternal Creator came to the cross—he who is God, blessed above all, forever.

[Col. 0267A]

## CHAPTER TWO  
### On the second figure, in which the holy cross is depicted within a quadrilateral

O holy cross of Christ, which, by the power bestowed upon you, excel above all things! You rule the heavenly hosts in the heights of heaven, powerful among the heavenly realm, because the power and divinity of the King crucified upon you made you wholly powerful and wholly holy, especially since the sign of his passion always remains upon you.

Therefore we rightly call you queen, by Christ the King, because through you we first obtained access to the heavenly kingdom. While bearing him, you merited both his human and divine grace; in the praise of the one almighty God, you joined together Christ’s worshipers in sacred confession.

For you stir up manifold praises to God among the holy assemblies of angels, and likewise [Col. 0267B] make the inhabitants of earth devoted to glorifying God. The whole world sanctifies you—air, sea, and the fiery stars of heaven—and every kind of creature from the four quarters of the world celebrates you with great devotion.

This unified confession of all likewise professes that, illumined by eternal light, you display to us the joys of the heavenly kingdom and grant them to those who devoutly seek what has been displayed. You do both by divine dispensation, so that with believing hearts and true confession we may confess Christ as God and through this faith may deserve to reach him.

O cross of Christ, blessed through his desired victory—how radiant and how great the Creator of all has made you through his love! He endowed you with the gift of giving life and mercifully raised you for this purpose, so that the ancient enemy, who expelled our first parent from paradise after he consented to him, might no longer weary his descendants, condemned in exile, with the mockery of his blessing.

O devout cross of the Lord, who is worthy to resound your praises in meter or to recount your entire power in words? You shine beautifully in your adornment and appear glorious to those who behold you. The deadly yew flees far from you; the aromatic reed and the evergreen pine subject themselves to your honor. The enduring cedar, impervious to worms, the flowing myrrh, and the sweet-smelling melilot [reading uncertain] marvel at your fragrance. Spikenard and fragrant cypress, mastic, the drop of lentisk, Arabian frankincense, the resin of India, Syrian amomum, balsam of Judea, and the bdellium of Phison, revering your majesty, exalt you above themselves with their vows. [Col. 0267D]

Although your name is harsher than theirs, since you resound the torment, yet by the power of our redemption you surpass them, granting the faithful the opportunity to receive the fruits of good works before Christ’s tribunal.

O sacred cross, which, breaking the bars of hell, rescued the people of the saints and established them in heaven!

## CHAPTER THREE  
### On the third form of the figure, in which the nine orders of angels are depicted

O holy salvation and joyful passion of Christ, hail! Venerable cross of God, you who are wisdom, light, and teacher of the world; true praise, friendly virtue, and radiant philosophy among the inhabitants of heaven and earth; you who flourish without end; and now among the armies [Col. 0268A] of angels who abide in the radiance of eternal light, and among human beings, for whom you became salvation and beautiful renewal after long weakness and the ancient decay of sins.

The whole world blesses you; the hosts of heaven praise you together. Through you, in the name of Jesus—who bends all the scepters of the world and the power of kings together—every knee bends, whether willingly or by force, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.

But Michael, leader and prince of God’s people, proclaims in confession that through you all the stars of heaven are both governed and protected by power, because you are God’s altar on which the Lamb who took away the sins of the world was sacrificed. With this shield of goodwill he continually rejoices; trusting in the sword of this confession, he begins battle against the dreadful dragon and the ancient [Col. 0268B] serpent. Triumphant over the enemy, he exults with thousands of the holy hosts, asking this as his reward: that he may sing your praise forever before the Lord’s tribunal.

Therefore the process of forming the letters, this arrangement of the nine orders, and the very order in which the angelic hosts were first arranged to praise the Redeemer rightly establish this cross, suspended in such a manner, as the altar of our high priest and Redeemer. Thus true life itself, bearing witness within it, may display the venerable senate of the virtues praising, as is fitting, so that upon the cross, which is our true salvation, good and salutary writings may appear.

For this reason Christ humbled himself and descended from the heights of heaven, so that he might firmly lead us to himself, the solid foundation of faith and the argument of all good things. He taught us by his words and left us examples through his deeds; and finally, redeeming us upon the holy cross, he brought his works to completion.

This, Gabriel, archangel of the Most High and arranger of the heavenly wedding, you joyfully revealed to the Virgin in clear speech when you announced the power of Christ’s kingdom and the work of his salvation in radiant language.

And you, Raphael, medicine of God: did you not, in that mystical work in which you opened Tobit’s eyes by anointing them with gall, signify the power of the holy cross, which, by the bitterness of Christ’s death, removed the darkness of sins and restored eternal light to the human race?

We must therefore believe that the deeds of the angels recounted by the Old Testament signify the coming and glory of our Redeemer, since the New Testament describes how, at the very beginning of his birth, the angels sang his glory in the highest with great rejoicing and proclaimed peace to human beings.

Therefore we also, illustrious armies of angels, humbly beseech you to offer fitting thanks without ceasing to our Savior and to bless his holy name forever: he who freed us through the cross from eternal death and filled your number in the heavenly heights with holy souls, so that it would not remain diminished because of the fallen angels.

## CHAPTER FOUR  
### On the form of the fourth design, where the cherubim and seraphim are depicted beside the cross

But you, heavenly companies, cherubim and seraphim, [Col. 0269A] now praise from heaven the name of your king Jesus Christ, because the fire of your love and wisdom burns so well when it shines with pure speech in praise of the Redeemer. True and divine is that praise by which our Passover—namely, the passion and resurrection of our Redeemer—is truly proclaimed to be our life. Christ is truly the fruit of light, whom, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, you celebrate in communal praise as Lord God Sabaoth. At the hour of his passion he conquered the sorrow of death, and now, reigning everywhere, he rejoices in the joy of resurrection.

O blessed seraphim, tell us what the burning of your love is; and if, in this celebration, the laws of your heavenly state are manifested, show whether you signify by this abundant and powerful praise the heavenly Victor.

Here I confidently answer on your behalf, both for myself and for my people. They show us one thing: by the position of their wings they affirm that the altar and sacred honor of the victim sacrificed upon it were long ago foretold to us in the figures of the holy cross.

They also proclaim Christ’s praises: the power of our redemption and the good rewards that Christ the King decreed to grant us. For when he suffered upon this altar according to his purpose, the flame of his passion consumed the iniquities and sins of our crimes. In an instant of his death he overcame and defeated all hostile powers; casting out the prince of this world, he broke open the destroyed bars of his prison and erased the ancientness of our sins. In his goodness, the Lord and [Col. 0269C] King of the virtues restored to us the very kingdoms of paradise in which the first human being had been created and placed.

The mouths of all the faithful confirm this, and the virtues and miracles that God performs in this world through his saints testify that God gave the human race—justly condemned to the prison and darkness of this world—the assistance of his commandments in order to escape perpetual death.

Our Creator and King, who was nailed for us to the high trunk of the cross: what is more fittingly called an imperial throne than a servile instrument of torture? For our emperor, King Christ, acquired for himself through it a kingdom and power in heaven and on earth; he overcame his enemies and reconciled the world to God. This is the standard of the Christian people; this is the sword with which we wage war against the enemy; this is the emblem of our victory. [Col. 0269D] With it we crush our enemies; with it we break the weapons of iniquity; through it we are lifted to the crown and receive the rewards of virtue.

Therefore, fire of desire, always exiled and estranged from the good, know what slaughter has been prepared for you in Christ’s death.

Those cherubim, then, who stood beside the altar in the construction of the tabernacle and temple, behind the altar of incense, by the extension of their wings—and by the entire arrangement of their position—displayed this standard of the cross and this holy altar. This holy altar, anointed with mystical unction, prefigured Christ’s triumph and the palm of his contest.

Thus these living creatures, that is, the cherubim, with their outstretched wings joyfully present Christ’s deeds and make it clear by evident signs that those deeds are blessed, gracious, and exalted. The seraphim also open their mouths for this purpose: while they proclaim that heaven and earth are full of God’s glory, they indicate that the time is already near when worldly luxury will depart from here and vices will recede.

Finally, let all things speak together. These living creatures, by the service of their wings, especially intimate that the Savior’s arms were extended upon the cross, and that through them all those whom he will later place in the blessed seat at the universal judgment are now drawn and raised up by mercy, when he renders to each according to his merits. Then he will openly test them by examination—those whom he has already recognized as his own and, through his love, proved enriched with good works.

The prophecies of the righteous seers concerning the Lord’s passion therefore in no way disagree, nor do the signs of these living creatures deceive.

## CHAPTER FIVE  
### On the form of the fifth figure, where four quadrilaterals stand around the cross

[Col. 0270B]

I now beseech you, holy cross of God, to bless my weak breast by your power, so that I may be able to sing in worthy praises the trophy of the eternal King in you: how you join heavenly and earthly things together in one covenant, confirm the pact, and dissolve the bonds of death.

O sacred company of the apostles and crowned order of martyrs, you rightly established the foundations of Christ’s house, whom he himself bears in the most beautiful heights. By your voice and examples you acquired a holy people for God, and rightly placed the holy and saving cross of Christ at the first foundation of your preaching, because the power of the Lord crucified upon it properly strengthened it to bear the whole structure of the Lord’s Church. [Col. 0270C]

Truly, the cross itself consecrated the human race to life and was erected as a firm column, desiring to show that through it the eternal house rises to be established in the heavenly kingdom—namely, the hall of the righteous King and Bridegroom of the Church.

You, Lord Christ, swiftly raised this new trophy in the world by the right of your dominion, the blood of redemption, and the way of guidance, so that the Christian people might preserve the covenant of justice, rightly despise the condemned devil, and overcome the hostile human being through devotion. For you are its supporter in praise, its safeguard and fear in preserving both good works, its palm of victory, and its crown of reward.

O illustrious cross of the Lord, precious foundation of Christ’s palace! You are more beautiful than the flowering appearance of all plants; higher than the cedars of Lebanon; more precious than Parian white stone. You join the squared stones of living stones together upon the firm foundation of faith.

The company of the patriarchs and the most ancient rite rightly laid the first foundations at the beginning of the entire building. By sound doctrine they first joined the devoted hearts of those obedient to them to the house of the God who reigns above all things through faith.

Afterward the prophets poured down words of preaching, so that by their admonitions and commands they might construct a living palace for King Christ at this place of combat. For this entire structure of the Church, through confession of the name of Jesus Christ, rises to the heavenly kingdom, and, built up by his word, the good construction of life rightly flourishes.

This conjunction of four quadrilaterals at the sides of the holy cross signifies and, by sacred [Col. 0271A] portent, reveals to us the meaning: we are to know by what straight way and under what excellent guide we are commanded to go—namely, to possess the everlasting kingdom. All those whom Christ’s visitation illumines by his dwelling, whom he deigns to dedicate as a temple, he will unite with these holy walls to himself as the cornerstone and bring to the perfection of the heavenly building.

## CHAPTER SIX  
### On the form of the sixth figure, where the four chief virtues are mentioned

Almighty power and the supreme wisdom of the almighty Father, Christ, Son of God, you are the true Lord who adorns the whole world with the beauty of the holy cross and piously dispenses to your saints the gracious gifts of salvation.

For the chariot of the virtues, fittingly joined to the four horns of the holy cross, displays the sacred sequence of forms proceeding from it, consecrated in the triumph of the King Christ’s victory. Through his beneficial passion it serves the whole world, for obtaining the fruit of devotion and attaining eternal blessedness.

Virtue is a disposition of the soul, an adornment of nature, a way of life, nobility of character, and moderation of speech. All these things, O holy cross, you offer for approval with just praise to religious people, bringing forth together all that pleases God and showing that each thing is salutary.

Your holy prudence taught the tender world from the beginning, when through the martyrdom of righteous Abel it showed that one must lay down one’s life for innocence. From you, justice, burning with good zeal, urged that the pomp of the devil be despised and that Christ’s grace be obeyed.

Through you, chaste love raises itself among God’s saints to pursue useful counsels, namely, the teaching of God’s commandments, so that it may remove the evil one’s deceit from the inner chambers of the human heart and teach God’s faithful, attentive to heavenly rewards, to overcome the desires of the flesh.

This same love leads holy preachers throughout the breadth of the world. They rebuke vices, commend virtues, and teach through the Gospel that thanks must be given to the Redeemer, who, according to the prophecy of the ancients, was made flesh in the last times and, giving evangelical commandments with signs and miracles, made himself known as the true God.

He granted all believers that through complete faith and baptism they might seek eternal light. To those who received heavenly teaching with attentive ears, he gave the ability, like good soil, to produce an abundant harvest of virtues from the seed of the word. If any incentives of nature arose within them, the knife of the Gospel would cut them away and the flame of the Holy Spirit would burn them, so that without any impediment they might offer the divine seed and spiritual delights to King Christ.

Faith and Christian religion first planted these fruits through the preachers of the Gospel; then the grace of the virtues displayed them as pure and free from every stain. Thereafter the patience of the saints tested them in tribulations; and the covenant and fellowship of true concord established them by showing them to be united and inseparable.

Then they are strongly strengthened by the virtue of steadfastness and preserved unharmed through true humility, so that by discernment they may advance toward increase and by patient perseverance reach fitting maturity.

After this, the sickle of the final judgment must be sent, so that the whitening harvest—which the grain of wheat, buried in the earth by the plow of the cross, has produced gloriously and abundantly—may be gathered, when the judge of the living and the dead appears, and by the sentence of that same righteous Judge may happily be placed in the heavenly granaries.

## CHAPTER SEVEN  
### On the form of the seventh figure, where the four elements are discussed

Therefore all things that are in heaven and on earth now shine, illumined by the light of Christ’s glory. Subject to his majesty, they serve him and celebrate together the work of the holy cross in blessing, so that they may render due vows to the heavenly Victor. They truly profess this: that all kingdoms preserve their proper order under the governance of Jesus’ divinity—not only those things that move throughout the world, but also all things that exist, live, perceive, discern, and know how to preserve their laws have stood under this dominion from the beginning.

Rain and hail from the clouds, snow, frost and ice, dew and clear weather, together with the springs and streams flowing over the earth, praise the Creator by bearing witness to him. The Cretan Bear [*Arcton Creticus*] and the entire arrangement of the stars, together with the turning of the pole, proclaim their author.

Let no one be displeased by what I say, for I write the praises of the All-Holding One and inflict neither mockery nor grief upon anyone. Bless the Lord, all the works of the Lord; sing and make melody to him.

Let the righteous praise him, saying that Christ, exalted upon the cross, draws all things to himself [Col. 0272C] and invites his chosen soldiers to the crown. For it is not right that his creation should be discordant in praising the Creator; rather, rejoicing, it should sing together the praises owed to him.

All things that swim in the waters and creep upon the earth; mountains and hills; the sand of the sea; groves and all the trees of the forests; wild animals, cattle, and fierce beasts; worms of the dust and tiny flying creatures; tame birds and those that tear with their claws.

O Christian people, by whom heaven and earth are adorned! From you the light of faith and the power of preaching proceed as an embassy to the nations; they stir up prayers and invite people to baptism. Above all, the speech of teachers, with splendid exhortation, uncovers the devil’s deceit and explains Christ’s victory to those acquired as elect through God’s grace.

This is preached daily to all the faithful, and likewise, with the greatest moderation and patience, it is made known to pagans, false Christians, and heretics. Whoever therefore believes the word of God will be saved; but whoever does not believe, or destroys faith through evil works, will be condemned forever.

Since Christ’s grace therefore overflows in heaven and on earth, it is entirely fitting that heavenly and earthly things together, with harmonious voice, sing praises and give thanks to God.

People of the Lord and sheep of his pasture, some of you already reign with the Lord in heaven, while others still journey on earth: one purpose urges you to praise God, for one joy awaits you in heaven. You already possess what has been given, and you will truly receive what has been promised, because the one who promised will undoubtedly fulfill his promises in you—your own King and Priest, Creator and Savior, Jesus Christ our Lord.

## CHAPTER EIGHT  
### On the form of the eighth design, where the meaning of the number twelve is explained

Christ, therefore, our Savior, Christ, the most gentle King, reigns in heaven: the best counsel, the supreme power of God the Father, and the true blessing; light from light, and divine offspring begotten from God the Father.

He is plainly the origin of all order. To this Craftsman the entire structure of heaven and earth looks; to him belongs every adornment of the virtues. From his goodness and truth comes everything good and true. He alone, wondrous, does wondrous things.

From his justice is ordered whatever is justly decreed, approved, and brought forth in heaven or on earth; whatever honor the good angels possess and whatever punishment the evil angels suffer; and likewise the fact that Christ expelled idolatry from the world and renewed divine worship.

The Lord Christ is therefore the author of all these good things, and on the standard of his cross he displays the judgments of his honor and power.

Therefore it is fitting that we, earthly beings and exiles from paradise, should mark these rays diffused by this form of the holy cross, through which Christ saves us and restores the splendor of light that the first-created human being once lost through sin.

All who, from the beginning, rightly recognized and venerated these rays enjoy the gift of perpetual light. The prophets’ weapons often flashed with this radiance, and the apostolic order, preaching, shone nobly with this light. By this sun the faith of Christ gleams throughout the world, and the good hearts of human beings and the pious vows of the saints are revealed.

The righteous, endowed with divine grace, through mystical signs once handed down to the fathers, cast forth a good and salutary ray. Accordingly, they persuade peoples to obey God’s commandments, attributing to Christ alone the power to reveal the depths of mysteries to the worthy and to bestow the gifts of eternal life upon the faithful.

Christ, therefore, the supreme King and Lord who grants heavenly things, ascending by divine gift the lofty beams of the cross, made it plainly known, by forming this design, that through it he opens the heavens to the world. He wishes us, following his footsteps, to find through it the entrance to life.

Finally, the four times three winds, joined and united from the four quarters of the world and the circuit of Ocean in the form of the holy cross, the Savior made healthful. As ruler, he sustains, governs, and directs the twelve signs together with their months, and he orders the twelve divisions of the hours to be drawn out and brought properly from sunrise to sunset.

To demonstrate all these things, the distribution of the number twelve completes the quadrangular form of the holy cross. For the cross of Christ, our glory, loosens all the bonds of our sins by which we were held fast; and, erected, it sets forth and marks the sacred joys of heaven and the laws of earth, praises and approves them, and truly grants them to the faithful.

[Col. 0274A]

## CHAPTER NINE  
### On the ninth figure, which contains the number of the days of the year in the form of a cross
Sun and moon, now bless the Lord Jesus Christ in fitting order, because the holy cross is your honor, steadfast light, ordered arrangement, sequence, praise, and excellence, illuminating you with spiritual light through all times. You too, by this number which it signifies in the four hexagons with a unit placed among them, count and balance the days and nights of the whole solar year, bringing your course to the perfection of that number. Thus the aforesaid figure contains thirty tens and ten sixes, and in addition five units. By these numbers, indeed, the wheel of the sun and moon is known to set its course; the four changes of the seasons are enclosed within them, and one year embraces them all together in fifty-two weeks and one unit. This order now holds the return of the two-faced [year]; toward this point the sequence of hours, the alternation of seasons, the annual circuit, and the course of the stars pass. The extra quarter-day, likewise exceeding the fixed number of days which the holy cross denotes in the arrangement of the six angles of the four hexagons, swiftly reaches that limit, as can properly be recognized at the equinoxes.

O sacred offspring, which illumines with the bright light of faith and wisdom the hearts of human beings placed in the darkness of unbelief: you are, clearly, the holy cross, sparkling with miracles. For Christ everywhere displays through your horns the breadth of his kingdom. You are the scepter of the mightiest king and the altar of the most high God; by your powerful order you spread throughout the world. You descended to the underworld and extend toward the heavenly realms. This is the glory and honor of the whole world. Our true Shem, likewise so named, through whose name alone the whole creation is saved, regulates the course of the stars according to this form and grants the kingdom of heaven, since, placed in this seat, he opens for us the bars of heaven.

For the human race sets this forth in songs of praise when it faithfully proclaims concerning Christ crucified by the Jews that at midday the light of the stars was darkened. For although Judaea, raging, seethed with envy, nevertheless brought forth this fruit for a better use from the tree of the cross: from the four regions of the world and from the quadriform rim of Ocean, nations and peoples flowing together from every side sought the spiritual delights displayed in the holy cross. Thus, filled with sacred and mystical banquets, through the gifts of the supreme Father they may attain the hundredfold fruit of good works, and, mingled with the splendid nine orders of angels, may themselves shine with perpetual brightness in heavenly blessedness.

Therefore I admonish you: whatever we sing and whatever we write, let us turn it all to the praise of the Redeemer, so that, by this one hope which we have through him and in him, repelling with the shield of faith the assault of greedy and raging death and of perpetual condemnation, we may escape; and thus, shining with the light above, may we joyfully deserve to possess the kingdom of God and to resound with worthy praises to our author and Redeemer, the Lord Jesus Christ, namely the Son of the almighty Father, true, holy, and most high Lord. Let this also always be our purpose: eternal praise and perpetual ardor of love.

## CHAPTER X. On the meaning of the tenth figure, where the reckoning of seventy is described

Now, therefore, it is fitting that sacred melody, making us joyful in hope of eternal things, should express in this blessed work what confers eternal life upon us, what removes corruption, what grants forgiveness of sins, and what breaks the bonds of sin—that is, that it should proclaim the deeds of the holy cross. Rightly, then, the human voice resounds this in the throat; the speaking mouth brings it forth by its art; the writing fingers, the plectrum of the tongue, and the vows of the devout heart proclaim it: namely, that the crooked and harmful dragon fell in battle, that one who by evil art, savage in paradise, deceived our first parent. For when Lucifer himself first fell, he dragged with him from the citadel of heaven a third part of the stars into the sulfurous pools of hell, because, proud and deceitful, he tried to make himself equal to the Most High, setting up his throne in the frozen region of the north.

This most savage wolf the gentlest Lamb laid low, by powerful right seized his prey, and shattered his immense designs. He also turned the nations from their deepest and carnal desires toward better things through the preaching of the holy Gospel, and kindled them toward heavenly gifts, lest either the fabulous superstition of the Jews or the perverse seduction of heretics should corrupt, under a beautiful covering, the chaste hearts of Christians. These, recognizing the truth of the divine law, already stand firm in the strength of faith. And lest the mouth of the nations, emptied of the worship of demons and the adoration of idols, should become dry, Christ the Lord, author of all good and giver of virtues, makes it fruitful in divine praise. For the powerful virtue of the holy cross both causes and condemns every faithlessness of the enemy; and, forgiving the world its debts, it surpasses all the riches of the wealthy by its gift.

Finally, that manifest redemption was contained in the number seventy, the prophet Daniel demonstrates in his seventy weeks, which reached as far as Christ: when transgression would be completed, sin would receive its end, iniquity would be blotted out, and everlasting righteousness would be brought in. Jeremiah likewise proclaims that, after seventy years, the release of captivity would come. Moses, however, through the seventy elders whom he placed over the people of Israel at the Lord’s command, signified that the perfection of all teaching and the revelation of mysteries are effected for us through the sacrament of the cross.

O blessed cross of God! In that you embrace the number seventy, divided into five parts, at your center, and likewise through your four horns by the numbers four and ten, you signify that through the ten words of the Law and through the four books of the holy Gospel you recall the whole world to harmony and unity of faith. Nor do you pass over the number five without mystery; rather, you reverently indicate that the human race is devoted to you most truly not only through the inward affection of the soul but also through the outward senses of the body.

## [Col. 0276A]

## CHAPTER XI. On the eleventh figure, where the Pentateuch of Moses is arranged

I invoke you, holy Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you may be my teacher and guide in this poem; that, gracious and merciful toward the work begun, you may grant understanding to its maker and bestow sober words, so that I may faithfully reveal, to the eternal praise of the holy cross and to the glory of the New Testament, what the ancient Law signifies in figures and what must now be observed spiritually in grace through the realities themselves.

For when this greatest structure of things was first made visible from invisible and impenetrable depth, and paradise appeared flourishing and delightful with its growth, immediately in the tree of life, which is in the midst of paradise, the life-giving tree of the holy cross was prefigured. Placed in the midst of the nations, it gives life and sanctifies the generations that preceded and follow it; through its benefit, all good and holy men, restored to life, bring forth spiritual and living fruits of virtue.

The patriarch Isaac likewise prefigured this tree of Christ’s passion when, with his father placing the wood upon his own shoulders, he carried it to the place of his sacrifice, as the book of Genesis testifies. So Exodus and the other books of the Law also explain that the holy cross, with its strong framework of arms, raised up our price, so that the heavenly Bridegroom might present to himself as bride the Church, without stain or wrinkle, as the dowry of his blood.

From here the people of Israel, joined to God in Egypt and led across the Red Sea, sang victorious praises to their Redeemer. Journeying for three days, with the Lord mercifully guiding them, they reached the spring of Marah, which was sweetened by the mystical wood. Thus Pharaoh and the Egyptians, who had pursued them and earlier mocked the people of God as though already captured and brought back, were submerged by the waves of the sea and, in belated repentance, lamented. But the Israelites, having seen the great wonders, sang a song of glory to their victorious leader, the God of their fathers, and, burning with love for their creator, rendered triumphant praises.

The eastern sea also bears witness to this, since to this day it preserves the tracks of the Egyptians’ chariots in its depths and on its shore. Finally, the holy cross, cast into the abyss of the ancient Law, sweetened it; and, cleaving the most solid rock, it brought forth a spring of living water. After its likeness Moses, extending his hands, won victory over Amalek, and through it the memory of the true Amalek was blotted out beneath heaven.

The two men who explored the land of promise and carried the cluster of grapes on a pole signify the two peoples, who proclaim that all believers can attain the joys above, accomplished through the passion of Christ on the cross.

O blessed cross of God! Who, knowing your mysteries well, can adequately recount such great and splendid gifts of salvation? No tongue of any creature is capable of celebrating the praises due to you. The sacrifice of the eternal Father, offered as a most fragrant odor, had consecrated you as a sacred altar. You exalted the serpent that gives life and displayed to the people the life-giving sign by which the wounded might be saved from their enemies. And what more can I say about you, except that you had given every good thing and taken away every evil?

## CHAPTER XII. On the meaning of the twelfth figure, where the name of the first parent is placed

Come now, sweet-sounding flute of metrical art; go and sing in gentle verses the saving praise of the Lord’s cross, and celebrate with devoted praises the wondrous work of our redemption and likewise the consolation of the life to come. For on the holy cross death was defeated most directly, and the bonds of our sins were loosed. Through Christ the former light returned to us, and forgiveness was granted for the first transgression.

The first Adam took away from us the beauty of immortality when, against the commandment, he tasted the fruit of the forbidden tree. The second Adam, namely our Savior, came and brought with him every beauty, every glory, and every honor of heavenly splendor. Because of the offense of one, we suffered many and innumerable evils and fell into the dangers of temporal death; likewise, because of the grace of one, the faithful multitudes are saved and obtain eternal light.

For just as through the tree of transgression death entered the whole world and all descended into hell, even the elect, so through the tree of the Lord’s passion death was taken captive, and many escaped from it, even those subject to sins. Christ opened through the cross an entrance to life for the entire world and displayed in it the power of his virtue; and, abandoning the worship of idols, he willed it to be honored by all. Through it he disclosed to us the secret of his sacrament and confirmed with us a covenant for keeping the right of his will.

The first man, earthly and from the earth, generated an earthly offspring and bequeathed to it a harsh death. The second, heavenly and from heaven, brought a heavenly generation into the world and promised his own an eternal blessedness. This is the Lord of all and creator of all things. He alone, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, possesses the eternal kingdom, and he wills the glorious assemblies of the saints to reign with him.

He also gave us an indication of his power, by which he rules throughout the whole world, through the name Adam, in which the four regions of the world are marked. For *anatole* [east], *dysis* [west], *arctos* [north], and *mesembria* [south], the four parts of the world, resound this in the initial letters of their names.

Therefore it is fitting that all living and existing things should acknowledge their Lord and sing together in devoted praises that Jesus Christ is the true Son of God and the almighty right hand of the almighty Father, whose healing is saving and whose touch is the medicine of eternal salvation.

## CHAPTER XIII. On the meaning of the thirteenth figure, where the number of days Christ remained in the Virgin’s womb is contained

Tree of most fragrant odor, exceedingly broad in the spreading of your beautiful leaves; incomparable garden of delights, abounding in the richest fertility; most pleasing in the flowers of virtues and the leaves of words; bearing fruit through the preachers of the holy Gospel—you store up heavenly riches. Exalted in majesty above all the trees of the forests, you stand honorable and beautiful, because the glory of Christ crucified upon you has displayed you as glorious, splendid, and venerable to all.

Whoever stands firm in faith openly professes this with complete devotion, although the dreadful power of the devil, begrudging the nations this salvation and their belief and knowledge of it, has thus far resisted. You display various forms of virtues in your bosom and signify that you possess an abundance of spiritual riches. You shine with the purple brilliance of Christ’s blood and strongly urge us to lay down our lives for Christ.

In you the exalted dignity of the Savior’s Churches stands, and the unity of the faithful will remain in faith and peace. The erection of the Mosaic tabernacle and the building of Solomon’s temple also prefigured this. The altar of burnt offering and of incense, and the fire always burning upon them, signified it; so did the lampstand with its four lamps and the rest of the Sabbath. For in Christ, the spotless Lamb of God sacrificed for our salvation on the altar of the cross, there are both the illumination of the faithful and the perpetual rest of the saints.

He is our forerunner to life through the passion of the cross; he is eternal salvation, true light, most devoted goodness, our redemption, and eternal life. He is the prince, like a son in his house—namely, the holy Church. He is our peace, who made both one. He destroyed the dominion of the devil and restrained his harmful efforts. The devil strives through the cold of unbelief to extinguish the warmth of charity; promising true happiness through the enticements of pleasures, he deceived the unwary, and, mocking them in this madness as though already captured, binds them with visible fetters of vices and chains of sins.

O holy cross! O beautiful tree, which surpasses all the groves of cedars in incomparable height and beauty! In the fitting number shining upon your horns, you signify the most serene and blessed gifts through the Lord’s coming. For you display the succession of days during which the Savior was incarnate in the Virgin’s womb, and through this period of his patience and humility you provide us with examples. And because he came to us through childbirth with gentleness and tranquility, you signify his meekness and obedience, which he preserved until death, accomplished upon you.

Therefore, according to his humanity, all power in heaven and on earth was given to him—the one who, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, created heaven and earth and all that is in them according to his divinity. As the holy prophets sang long ago, the maker of heaven and earth would be born as a little child, whose dominion would be upon his shoulder.

## CHAPTER XIV. On the fourteenth figure, in which the number of years from the beginning of the world to the year of Christ’s Passion is marked

Truly it is a worthy and exceedingly splendid work to sing with sweet-sounding melody the triumph of the heavenly King; to proclaim fittingly the triumph of the eternal ruler, by which he rescued the world from the power of the tyrant, and, after destroying and restoring his kingdom, condemned him to eternal imprisonment. In this kingdom he also upholds and sustains heavenly, earthly, and maritime things, having acquired them for himself.

For when his exaltation from the origin of the world’s birth is considered, the number of years, advancing with its mystery, expresses it through the Greek letters arranged in the figure itself.
